newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Resigned Palestinian minister calls U.S. "cowboy".
newsitem.headline: Resigned Palestinian minister calls U.S. "cowboy".

text.p: A Palestinian lawyer accused Washington on Tuesday of acting like a rude cowboy with a Zionist attitude for saying no tears were being shed over his resignation as Yasser Arafat's justice minister.
Freih Abu Meddein had angered the United States, Israel and rights groups by campaigning to execute Palestinians who sell land to Israelis. He quit this week in a dispute over political appointments.
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters in Washington on Monday: "I'm not sure there are many tears being shed" over the minister's departure.

In response Abu Meddein told Reuters: "Actually it's none of their business but it is the rudeness of the cowboy. The American administration is led by the Zionist concept. Therefore it works against the interests of the nations."

Abu Meddein announced in May that the PLO had revived a Jordanian military law banning the sale to Jews of land in the occupied Gaza Strip and West Bank, including East Jerusalem, upon penalty of death.
The law was adopted to prevent Jewish settlement expansion that has plunged Israel-PLO peacemaking into crisis.

Since then, the Palestinian Authority has detained more than 20 suspected land dealers and three more have been found dead. Israel has blamed the Authority for the deaths, but Palestinian officials denied any involvement.

The United States has spoken out strongly against what it called "political assassination against people who sell land to Israelis." While Arafat some time ago also strongly opposed such violence, Burns said with Abu Meddein's departure "perhaps that prospect is more sure now."

Abu Meddein said on Tuesday he resigned because of a disagreement over some appointments. But he said these did not include Arafat's appointment of attorney-general Fayez Abu Rahmeh on Saturday, as some officials had suggested.
A PLO official said Arafat had yet to accept the resignation. Abu Meddein remains a Palestinian legislator.
